title: Io sono, tu sei: il verbo essere
summary: Subject pronouns, the verb essere, the tu/Lei split, and why Italian usually drops the pronoun

blocks.title: The people words
blocks.body: *io* (I), *tu* (you, informal), *lui* (he), *lei* (she), *noi* (we), *voi* (you all), *loro* (they). One special job: **Lei** with a capital L means a **formal 'you'** to one person — used with strangers and in polite situations. It borrows the 'she' form, so *Lei è…* = 'you (formal) are…'.
blocks.callout: *tu* for friends and peers. *Lei* for strangers, shopkeepers, older or formal contexts.

blocks.title: essere — to be (learn this cold)
blocks.body: *essere* is irregular and everywhere. **io sono, tu sei, lui/lei è, noi siamo, voi siete, loro sono.** Note *io sono* and *loro sono* look the same — context tells them apart.

blocks.title: Drop the pronoun
blocks.body: The verb ending already tells you who — so Italian usually **drops the subject pronoun**. You say *Sono di Roma*, not *Io sono di Roma*. Keep the pronoun only for **contrast or emphasis**: *Io sono di Roma, e tu?* ('I'm from Rome — and you?').
blocks.callout: Default: no pronoun. Add *io/tu* only to point or contrast.

blocks.prompt: Which is the most natural way to say 'I'm from Milan'?
blocks.explain: *Sono di Milano.* The ending -o already means 'I', so the pronoun *io* is dropped.

blocks.title: tu vs Lei — same question, two registers

pairs.note: tu uses the tu-form *sei*; Lei uses the è-form. Match it to who you're talking to.

blocks.explain: *Siamo amici.* No pronoun needed — *siamo* already means 'we are'.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type. (It means 'Are you Italian?')

blocks.scene: Marco introduces you to a new face at the bar — a quick who-are-you exchange

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.nl: Lei è Giulia, una mia amica.
lines.en: This is Giulia, a friend of mine.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Ciao Giulia! Io sono canadese, di Toronto.
lines.en: Hi Giulia! I'm Canadian, from Toronto.
lines.spotlight: Here the *io* is kept — you're contrasting yourself with the others.

lines.speaker: Giulia
lines.nl: Ah, che bello! E sei qui a Bologna adesso?
lines.en: Oh, lovely! And you're here in Bologna now?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Sì, sono qui da poco. Sto imparando l'italiano.
lines.en: Yes, I've been here a short while. I'm learning Italian.

blocks.prompt: Introduce yourself with essere: where you're from, and whether you're new here. Try dropping the pronoun where you can.
